2609.04915.title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering and Atom-Aware Packing
2609.04915.paper_summary:
Many long-horizon LLM deployments face tight prompt budgets: latency, cost, and context limits make full-context prompting impractical as interaction length grows. The key question is then not raw recall alone, but which memory design gives the best quality--token trade-off in the compact-memory regime. We present \textbf{RSM-full}, an online clustered-memory pipeline designed for a strong quality--token Pareto point.
  RSM-full combines two design choices: a cosine-gated \emph{max-member merge} write rule and an atom-aware grouped context packer. On AMA-Bench, our primary compact-memory benchmark, it reaches $83%$ of Full-Context quality at $32%$ of the token cost at a $4$k budget; under four-seed averaging it beats the closest streaming-clustered baseline (Online K-Means) by $+3.5$--$6.0$,pp ($p{<}.001$) across the whole ${\sim}2.6$k--${\sim}5$k regime. Three-seed ablations show most of this gain comes from the merge rule ($+5.7$,pp over Online K-Means and matched-$τ$ DP-means) and the grouped packer ($+5.0$,pp over flat concatenation).
  The pattern reproduces on RealMem, an independent long-horizon persona-memory benchmark: RSM-full improves on Budget-RAG ($+0.69$,pp, $p{=}.006$), is on par with BM25-RAG (paired $Δ{=}{+}0.27$,pp, $p{=}.47$; we do \emph{not} claim BM25 equivalence in the equivalence-test sense), and significantly outperforms Streaming-Proto ($+2.97$,pp) and the closest reproduced 2025 agentic-memory baseline A-MEM ($+1.65$,pp, $p{<}.001$). Across benchmarks the message is consistent: under tight budgets, compact-memory performance is driven mainly by how streaming memories are merged and how retrieved content is assembled.
  Overall, RSM-full is most useful when answeroughly $2k$--$5k$ prompt tokens, where itdefines a strong compact-memory Pareto point; higher-token baselines remain stronger outside this regime.
2609.04915.paper_summary_zh:
許多長期部署的 LLM 面臨緊湊的提示預算：延遲、成本和上下文限制使得隨著互動長度的增加，完全上下文提示變得不切實際。關鍵問題不僅僅是原始回憶，而是在哪種記憶設計下能在緊湊記憶範疇內提供最佳的質量—令牌權衡。我們提出了 \textbf{RSM-full}，這是一個在線聚類記憶管道，旨在實現強大的質量—令牌 Pareto 點。<lb/>  
RSM-full 結合了兩個設計選擇：一個餘弦門控的 \emph{max-member merge} 寫入規則和一個原子感知的分組上下文打包器。在我們的主要緊湊記憶基準 AMA-Bench 上，它在 $4$k 預算下達到了 $32\%$ 的令牌成本下的 $83\%$ 完全上下文質量；在四種種子平均下，它比最近的流式聚類基線（在線 K-Means）高出 $+3.5$--$6.0$ pp ($p{<}.001$)，在整個 ${\sim}2.6$k--${\sim}5$k 範疇內。三種種子消融實驗顯示，這一增益大部分來自於合併規則（比在線 K-Means 和匹配的 $τ$ DP-means 高出 $+5.7$ pp）和分組打包器（比平坦串接高出 $+5.0$ pp）。<lb/>  
這一模式在獨立的長期個性記憶基準 RealMem 上得到了重現：RSM-full 在 Budget-RAG 上有改進（$+0.69$ pp, $p{=}.006$），與 BM25-RAG 相當（配對 $Δ{=}{+}0.27$ pp, $p{=}.47$；我們不聲稱 BM25 在等價測試意義上的等價性），並且顯著超越了 Streaming-Proto（$+2.97$ pp）和最近重現的 2025 年代理記憶基線 A-MEM（$+1.65$ pp, $p{<}.001$）。在各基準中，信息是一致的：在緊湊預算下，緊湊記憶的性能主要取決於流式記憶的合併方式和檢索內容的組裝方式。<lb/>  
總體而言，RSM-full 在大約 $2k$--$5k$ 提示令牌時最為有用，因為它定義了一個強大的緊湊記憶 Pareto 點；在此範疇之外，高令牌基線仍然更強。
